description: Checks which conditions for security for costs in the civil courts of England and Wales (CPR Part 25 Section VI, as rewritten from 6 April 2025) appear to be met on your answers, with the rule's words: a claimant resident out of the jurisdiction (with the enforcement position by country, including the 2019 Hague Judgments Convention), a company with reason to believe it will be unable to pay (and after-the-event insurance), a change of address to evade, no or an incorrect address, a nominal claimant, steps taken with assets, funders and assignors (r.25.28), appeals (r.25.29), counterclaims, Solicitors Act and detailed assessments, arbitration challenges (s.70(6)) and foreign judgment registrations (CPR 74.5); then the discretion factors and the procedure. It never decides the application and never suggests an amount of security: that is for the court.

address.description: The address in the claim form: "correct" (given, and correct), "none" (not given), "incorrect" (incorrect).

aos.description: Whether the party applying has filed an acknowledgment of service or a defence (against a counterclaim, a defence to it): "yes" or "no".

appealTarget.description: "appeal": who security is sought from: "appellant" (the appellant), "cross-appellant" (a respondent who also appeals), "respondent" (a respondent who does not appeal).

applicant.description: "claim" or "solicitors-act": who is applying for security: "defendant" (the defendant), "counterclaim" (the claimant, as defendant to a counterclaim), "claimant" (the claimant, against a defendant who only defends).

arbTarget.description: "arbitration": whether security is sought from the party challenging or appealing the award: "yes" or "no".

assets.description: Whether they have taken steps with their assets that would make a costs order hard to enforce: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

assetsHere.description: The claimant has assets or a fund in England and Wales.

assignPurpose.description: Where "assignor": whether the claim was assigned to avoid a costs order against them: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

ate.description: After-the-event insurance: "none" (none), "unprotected" (a policy the insurer could avoid), "protected" (anti-avoidance terms or a deed of indemnity).

capacity.description: Whose benefit the claim is for: "own" (their own), "nominee" (someone else's: a nominee with no real interest), "representative" (an estate or trust), "part19" (a group: a Part 19 representative claimant).

costsOrderAgainst.description: Where someone else is behind the claim: whether a costs order could be made against them: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

counterclaim.description: The defendant has a counterclaim on the same issues.

defendantCaused.description: The claimant says the defendant caused its lack of means.

evade.description: Where moved: whether there is evidence the move was to evade the consequences of the litigation: "yes" or "no".

issued.description: The date the claim was issued, for the 2019 Hague Judgments Convention (Art 16) (YYYY-MM-DD).

judgment1982.description: "foreign-judgment": whether the registration is under the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

kind.description: The party security is sought from: "individual" (an individual), "company" (a company or other body).

limited.description: That company is a limited company (for r.25.29(2) on an appeal).

moved.description: Whether the address has changed since the claim was commenced: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

nomineeUnable.description: Where "nominee": whether there is reason to believe the nominee will be unable to pay: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

permission.description: "appeal": permission to appeal: "granted" (granted), "adjourned" (adjourned to a hearing, appeal to follow).

proceeding.description: What the security is for: "claim" (a claim, or a counterclaim, at first instance), "appeal" (an appeal), "assessment" (a detailed assessment between the parties), "solicitors-act" (a Solicitors Act assessment of a solicitor's bill), "arbitration" (a challenge or appeal under the Arbitration Act 1996, ss.67 to 69), "foreign-judgment" (registering a foreign judgment, or setting the registration aside).

stifling.description: The claimant says an order would stifle the claim.

thirdParty.description: Anyone else behind the claim: "none" (no one), "funder" (a funder paying for a share of any recovery), "assignor" (someone who assigned the claim to the claimant), "backer" (someone paying towards the costs without a share).

unable.description: A company: whether there is reason to believe it will be unable to pay the costs if ordered to: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

vitality.description: Against a counterclaim: whether it has a life of its own, beyond defending the claim: "yes", "no" or "unsure".

where.description: Where they live, or for a company where it is managed and controlled: "england-wales" (England and Wales), "scotland" (Scotland), "northern-ireland" (Northern Ireland), "eu" (An EU member state other than Denmark), "denmark" (Denmark), "switzerland" (Switzerland), "ukraine" (Ukraine), "uruguay" (Uruguay), "albania" (Albania), "montenegro" (Montenegro), "andorra" (Andorra), "elsewhere" (Anywhere else (for example the USA, the BVI, China, Kenya, the UAE)).

name: check_security_for_costs
title: Security for costs checker (CPR 25.26 to 25.29)
